title: Make a complaint about a lawyer or barrister
summary: This page provides information on how to complain about the service or conduct of a lawyer or barrister in NSW, starting with direct resolution and escalating to the Office of the NSW Legal Services Commissioner (OLSC).
intro:
You may have issues with the service or conduct of a lawyer (solicitor or barrister) in NSW. If so, the first step is to speak with them and try to resolve the matter.

If you cannot resolve the matter, the Office of the NSW Legal Services Commissioner (OLSC) can help you.

who_can_apply: Having an issue with the service or conduct of a lawyer (solicitor or barrister) in NSW.

more_info.text: Once you make a complaint, it may take up to 8 weeks for a case officer to assess the issue.
The resolution process can take time, sometimes up to a year.

faqs.q: What should I do if I have an issue with my lawyer?
faqs.a: First, try to speak with the lawyer directly to resolve the matter. If you cannot resolve it, the Office of the NSW Legal Services Commissioner (OLSC) can help.

faqs.q: What types of issues can the OLSC help with?
faqs.a: The OLSC can assist with various issues related to legal services.
